blindSummary:
This state/province is the only one in the country's religious-law belt with a carried-out death-by-stoning sentence for same-sex acts in the modern record: on 28 June 2022 a religious court in a rural local-government area sentenced three men to death under the moral-offences provision of the state's 2001 religious penal law, following arrest by the religious-morality police on 14 June 2022 and conviction on their own admissions; the morality-police chief publicly announced the case. Lower-level practice includes secret floggings (March 2014, four men 15 lashes each, trial held in secret) and a religious commission charging a dozen men with belonging to a "gay club" (January 2014). LGBT+ groups warned the stoning could trigger similar cases across the belt.

Mitigating institutional fact: the state's senior religious appellate court has repeatedly quashed stoning sentences on appeal (two 2003 convictions reversed - one for denial of counsel and a defective confession - and a third appeal then pending in another belt state), per an international rights organisation's 2004 release, which noted "a number of cases where convictions and sentences to death have been quashed on appeal". However, the 2022 conviction and public announcement demonstrate active enforcement capacity with a capital outcome - documented nowhere else in the country.
